summary: Carroll County, OH tower put up by the Ohio Division of Forestry in 1951 as an 80-foot steel tower; listed as gone, and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: 80-foot steel tower with a wooden cab, per an April 1951 newspaper report
facts.status_note: Listed as gone on the Ohio list of the Forest Fire Lookout Association
facts.agency: Ohio Division of Forestry, per the 1951 newspaper report

events.note: Completed the week before an April 18, 1951 newspaper report; 80-foot steel tower with a wooden cab; one of five the division erected in eastern Ohio
Tower man on duty on dry windy days in spring and fall; Alpha Moreland of RD 1 named for set days

evidence.supports: Tower site is in Carroll County, Ohio
Tower completed the week before the April 18, 1951 report
New 80-foot tower on a hill overlooking Leavittsville
evidence.quote: a new 80-foot fire tower erected on a hill overlooking Leavittsville in Carroll co.

evidence.supports: One of five towers erected in eastern Ohio by the Ohio Division of Forestry
evidence.quote: is one of five erected in eastern Ohio by the Ohio Division of Forestry

evidence.supports: Tower guarded a tree-planting area east of New Philadelphia planted by the Muskingum Conservancy District
evidence.quote: Protection against forest fires in the area east of New Philadelphia where thousands of trees have been planted by the Muskingum Conservancy District

evidence.supports: Steel tower with a wooden cab
evidence.quote: The Leavittsville tower is made of steel with a wooden cab

evidence.supports: Tower is on land the state leased
evidence.quote: leased on land leased by the state

evidence.supports: Tower man on duty on dry windy days in spring and fall
evidence.quote: The tower man will be on duty on dry windy days in the spring and in the fall

evidence.supports: The district forester called the spring and fall the most dangerous fire period
Alpha Moreland named as staffing the tower on set days
evidence.quote: manned on specific days by Alpha Moreland of RD 1

evidence.supports: Forester hoped to equip all towers with radios by fall
evidence.quote: By fall we hope to have all the towers equipped with radios

evidence.supports: Watcher had to leave the tower to check a fire and then report it
evidence.quote: the tower man will have to leave the tower to investigate any fires

evidence.supports: Ohio list marks the tower as gone; register number US 1564, OH 10
evidence.quote: Leavittsville Carroll 40.51165 -81.19334 Tower Gone FFLOS US 1564, OH 10

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register page and the Ohio list both give US 1564, OH 10; they describe the same tower, so the shared number is not a conflict

notes_for_editor: Built and staffing rest on one newspaper clip quoted on the Forest Lookouts page. 'Gone' rests on the Ohio list alone; no source gives a removal date or describes the site today. No access information found, so no access key. The brief's register number note was checked and is not a conflict.
